The Operator has failed to comply with the conditions set forth in the Order and is therefore in violation of OGA3259(1).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/15/2025 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Charleston Township, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/15/2025
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8252998
Permit API: 117-20505
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Charleston Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/15/2025
Comments: On 10/15/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 49 degrees and overcast when I arrived on site. Rainfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Prior to this inspection, Seneca personnel had told me that a construction crew was being mobilized to the site to restore the pad back to well pad condition, repairing the spots that were excavated after the release discovered on 5/13/2025. When I arrived on site I did witness some construction equipment at the site. The area that was excavated around and north of the well cellars remains open along with the areas on the fill slope and across the grassy field north of the pad. A Gas Field Specialist crew was on site digging an 8-foot-deep trench across the pad north of the well cellars. Short, downward sloping trenches from each well cellar would be installed to the long trench and then layered with gravel. Clean out pipes will be installed on the east and west end of the long trench with another one in the center. Liquids coming from the well cellars could be monitored in this trench and collected if necessary. A different construction company will be repairing the rest of the pad.Field conductivity readings taken during this inspection are as follows: Liquid on the northeast corner of the pad being 1.066 mS conductance or less. Liquid below the west disturbed area on the fill slope being 0.769 mS conductance. Liquid flowing down from the east fill slope disturbed area being 1.212 mS conductance. Liquid in the sump pit at the northwest corner of the location being 1.315 mS conductance. This fluid was being pumped up to the pad surface into a frac tank on the pad. Soil probe readings taken below the rock lined swale on the west side of the pad being 0.501 mS conductance or less.There are four active wells on site staged for production, along with one plugged well and one that is in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H well has a monument with plugged date of 12/4/2024. The 5H well has not been successfully plugged yet. The production tanks and GPUs are staged in secondary containment.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed below the excavated areas.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 399274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1000 hours.

A Gas Field Specialist crew was on site digging an 8-foot-deep trench across the pad north of the well cellars. Short, downward sloping trenches from each well cellar would be installed to the long trench and then layered with gravel. Clean out pipes will be installed on the east and west end of the long trench with another one in the center. Liquids coming from the well cellars could be monitored in this trench and collected if necessary. A different construction company will be repairing the rest of the pad.Field conductivity readings taken during this inspection are as follows: Liquid on the northeast corner of the pad being 1.066 mS conductance or less. Liquid below the west disturbed area on the fill slope being 0.769 mS conductance. Liquid flowing down from the east fill slope disturbed area being 1.212 mS conductance. Liquid in the sump pit at the northwest corner of the location being 1.315 mS conductance. This fluid was being pumped up to the pad surface into a frac tank on the pad. Soil probe readings taken below the rock lined swale on the west side of the pad being 0.501 mS conductance or less.There are four active wells on site staged for production, along with one plugged well and one that is in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H well has a monument with plugged date of 12/4/2024. The 5H well has not been successfully plugged yet. The production tanks and GPUs are staged in secondary containment.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed below the excavated areas.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 399274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1000 hours.

properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/07/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Columbia, Springfield and Troy Townships, Bradford County on 8/7/2025 at 0900 hours. The weather was 68 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted to assess ongoing remedial activities after a well control incident on 7/13/2025 resulted in a produced fluids release.Repsol continues to conduct remedial activities. Some scraping and removal of pad material around the western corner of the pad surface has been conducted. Materials removed from the pad and soils removed from impacted areas downslope are being stored within a secondary containment structure on the pad (photo #1). Repsol has obtained approval to dispose of impacted materials at a landfill. A rain event occurred on Thursday, 7/31/2025. Stormwater and fluids are being diverted into the lined detention basin located downslope of the pad (photo #12). Less than 6 inches of fluids were observed in the basin today. Drain tile piping has been installed downslope of the majority of the pad's fill slopes (photos #2, 3, 7 and 9) that divert collected fluids into the lined channels (photos #5 and 10) that then flow to the lined detention basin (photo #12). The drain tile piping outlets can be seen in photos #6 and 10. The "secondary" and "tertiary" emergency berms that were constructed following the release have been reworked (photo #8). The "tertiary" berm was determined to not have been impacted. The channel in the bottom of the "secondary" berm was excavated and impacted materials were removed.A water truck continues to collect fluids from the preexisting stormwater basin (photo #11) as necessary. Repsol plans to have a stationary pump brought in to pump fluids collected in the stormwater basin into the lined detention basin. A crew worked today to install a 4-inch line that will eventually pump fluids collected in the lined detention basin into a storage tank held on the pad surface. Fluids will only be held in the 4-inch line when pumping from the basin is ongoing. Three shallow, monitoring wells have been drilled downslope of the well pad to monitor the groundwater (see photo #14 for example). A fourth shallow, monitoring well is planned to be drilled in the adjacent field. Four deep, monitoring wells will also be drilled at the same locations as the shallow ones. Repsol reported that the first samples from the three monitoring wells already drilled may be collected today, 8/7.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the Seneca Resources - Cruttenden 846 Well Site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 8/19/22 @1230 hours in response to notification of the release of 20 gallons of produced fluid to surface of the Cruttenden 846 water pad. The weather was 82 degrees, mostly sunny. Activity onsite consists of stimulation of the 30HU well.Mr. Doug Kepler, Seneca Resources notified the DEP after-hours of a release of 20 gallons of produced fluid to the pad surface from a vac truck. As of today's inspection, Mr. Adam Pierce, Seneca Completions Consultant was present onsite. Mr. Pierce stated yesterday evening two drivers from the same company were offloading, when the one driver assumed the other was done and prematurely unhooked his hose while there was still fluid in the hose. He rushed the hose into the containment, but lost about 20 gallons of produced fluid in the process. Mr. Pierce estimated the impacted area to be approximately 12' wide and radiating out from the secondary containment approximately 4' in a half circle. Standing liquid was recovered with a vac truck and impacted pad material was removed with a skid steer. Mr. Pierce stated approximately 4 skid steer bucket loads of material were excavated. He estimated they excavated down approximately 2" to remove the visibly damp material. The material was observed staged inside the produced fluid tanks secondary containment until proper disposal could be arranged. Some of the material appeared visibly damp with a field measured conductivity of >4.0mS/cm. I asked if the excavated area was screened with a field conductivity meter to ensure the impacted pad material had been fully removed before backfilling with clean material. Mr. Pierce stated they did not possess a field condutivity meter onsite and had removed any visually impacted material. The spill area appeared fully remediated at the time of this inspection. Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED at this time against the 30HU well API#117-22125:CSL 402(b)SWMA30125 PA Code 78a.64a(b)I departed the site at 1345 hours.

The results of this monitoring indicated that 0% LEL and 0% Methane was measured during the inspection. Violations are continued from original date of 5/01/2025. Comments: On January 16, 2019, the Department performed an inspection of the EQT/Rice Drilling B Great Tiger well pad site. The site is located in Aleppo Twp., Greene Co. The inspection was related to a reported release of Brine to the well pad by the operator. The operator reported on 1/14/19 at 19:52, a 15 gallon brine spill at the Rice Drilling B - Great Tiger location, to the Department spill hotline. Operator reported that the spill was noticed at 19:00. On January 16, 2019 the Department spoke to the operator on the phone for further information. The operator reported that a seal on a valve in the A side GPU for well#596397 (API# 059-27199) failed causing a release of approximately 30 gallons of brine from the GPU. 15 gallons was contained within the unit and 15 gallons was estimated to be released to the well pad. The operator stated that the LEL monitor in the GPU must have also malfunctioned, because it was to shut the well in upon detecting the gas release. The low and high level gas flow monitors in the GPU also did not shut in the well, upon the release. The operator stated that SPSI was dispatched to the site and excavated visually impacted material from the well pad. The Department investigated the spill and new stone had been placed around the failed GPU unit on the well pad. None of the GPUs on the site are in secondary containment, as required by § 78a.64a(b).

Comments: December 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill reported to the Department on 10/20/2023 (CTS: 375673). According to the operator, the spill was approximately 40 barrels of production fluid, released from the valve near the bottom of the production tank. The initial inspection of the spill is documented in IR 3636824. The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.

Comments: On 3/14/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Martin 2 gas well, API 129-27948. The well appeared equipped for production. The well displayed moderate corrosion. The well name and API was scratched into a pipe clamp, this does not meet the posting requirements of 3211(G). The line leading to the production tank appears to have failed and separated. A second tank was unused onsite as seen in the photographs, it is recommended to remove this equipment under OGA 3216(c). OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 611 and detected multiple gas leaks. Gas was leaking from the base of the wellhead as seen in the attached photographs at 12%LEL. The line leading into the production tank appears to have separated and was leaking gas at 79%Gas. The soils in a 2' radius around the failed connected were tested and gas was detected at a peak of 31%LEL in the soils at 3" depth. No 2023 APR is on record, the latest record is from 2022 and indicates production. No 2023 MIA is on record, the latest record is from 2022. Based on todays inspection the following violations will be issued: OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department. 78.88(d) - Failure to notify the Department and take corrective action to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion or other signs of deterioration that compromises the integrity of the well. 78.73(a) - Failure to operate the well in accordance with 25 PA code Chapter 78 and ensure the integrity of the well is maintained. 78.74 - Venting of gas to the atmosphere that produces a hazard to public health and safety.

Comments: On 3/14/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Martin 2 gas well, API 129-27948. The well appeared equipped for production. The well displayed moderate corrosion. A second tank was unused onsite as seen in the photographs, it is recommended to remove this equipment under OGA 3216(c). OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 611 and detected multiple gas leaks.
